response.sql:
WITH order_item_town_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    ili.order_item_id,
    c.town_city,
    AVG(ili.product_price) as item_avg_price,
    AVG(ili.derived_product_cost / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) as item_avg_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  JOIN Invoices i ON ili.invoice_number = i.invoice_number
  JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city
),
town_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    town_city,
    AVG(item_avg_price) as avg_product_price,
    AVG(item_avg_ratio) as avg_cost_ratio
  FROM order_item_town_avg
  GROUP BY town_city
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_cost_ratio) as overall_avg_ratio
  FROM town_avg
)
SELECT 
  ta.town_city,
  ta.avg_product_price,
  ta.avg_cost_ratio,
  ta.avg_cost_ratio - oa.overall_avg_ratio as ratio_above_average
FROM town_avg ta
CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
WHERE ta.avg_cost_ratio > oa.overall_avg_ratio
ORDER BY ta.town_city;

assumptions.assumption: Rows where derived_total_cost is zero or NULL are excluded from ratio calculation to avoid division by zero; NULL values in product_price and derived_product_cost are ignored per SQL AVG default behavior

Each order_item_id may appear across multiple invoice line items (partial invoicing). The request's two-step process ('for each order item id and town' first, 'then average those per town') means order_item_ids with few line items have equal weight to those with many, not weighted by invoice count

alternatives.interpretation: If the request intends to average product_price and ratio directly at the town level without the intermediate per-order_item_id step, giving higher weight to order_item_ids with more invoiced instances
